<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

I don't think the premise holds for the elements in the test. Step 1 of [determining the target of an event handler](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#determining-the-target-of-an-event-handler) is:

> If *eventTarget* is not a `body` element or a `frameset` element, then return *eventTarget*.

and all three cases operate on a `div`, so the target is the element itself rather than null — the setter storing the value is what the spec asks for, and browsers match it.

Even a `body` wouldn't return null with this handler: step 2 returns *eventTarget* unless the name is a `WindowEventHandlers` member or in the `Window`-reflecting body element event handler set, which is just `onblur`, `onerror`, `onfocus`, `onload`, `onresize` and `onscroll`.

That narrower case already has coverage in `event-handler-attributes-windowless-body.html`, which asserts the getter returns null and the setter is ignored for those names — and that handlers which aren't shadowed, such as `onclick`, work normally on a windowless `body` in a `DOMParser` document. That's the opposite of what the new test asserts for a `div` in the same kind of document, so the two contradict each other.

https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63110 corrects it. It also fixes two unrelated bugs there: the content attribute body assigned to a local variable `run_checks` can't see, so the check was vacuous; and `new Document()` is an XML document, so `innerHTML` used XML fragment parsing and left the `div` in no namespace, where it has no `onclick` IDL attribute at all.

Unless `event-handler-attributes-windowless-body.html` is failing somewhere, I don't think there's a spec/engine gap left here and this can be closed.

</details>
Yes, this was a misreading of the spec. Thanks!
